articles.title: Graphic Fonts CVE-2026-119969 shows why content parsers need patch evidence
articles.excerpt: Graphic Fonts CVE-2026-119969 shows why content parsers need patch evidence Fonts are executable input to a rendering stack. A malformed font can exercise table parsing, glyph transforms and memory ma…
articles.body: Graphic Fonts CVE-2026-119969 shows why content parsers need patch evidence Fonts are executable input to a rendering stack. A malformed font can exercise table parsing, glyph transforms and memory management long before a document is displayed. Microsoft's November 2026 Graphic Fonts advisory assigns CVE-2026-119969 an 8.8 base score and describes a remote code execution vulnerability. The public title identifies the affected component and the outcome. The available record does not explain the precise malformed structure or the memory-safety primitive. Defenders should keep that uncertainty visible. A broad statement that every font file can execute code is inaccurate. A broad statement that font parsing is harmless is also wrong.

articles.title: How QR Code Cashback Systems Work: Unique Codes, Fraud Checks and UPI Payouts
articles.excerpt: Cashback used to mean one thing: a percentage back on a card or wallet payment. In India, a newer model is growing fast. Brands print a unique QR code on every pack, the buyer scans it after purchase,…
articles.body: Cashback used to mean one thing: a percentage back on a card or wallet payment. In India, a newer model is growing fast. Brands print a unique QR code on every pack, the buyer scans it after purchase, and money lands in their UPI account within minutes. It looks simple from the outside. Under the hood it is a small but interesting system that has to solve code generation, fraud, and payouts at scale. This post walks through how a typical QR cashback platform is put together. 1. Generating codes that cannot be guessed Every pack needs its own code, and those codes must be impossible to predict. If codes were sequential, anyone could script a loop and claim thousands of rewards.

articles.title: Why Selling a $5 Digital Product Costs You Up to 31% in Fees
articles.excerpt: Impulse pricing feels like the easiest way to make your first dollar online. You ship a Notion template, an icon pack, a CLI utility, or a starter boilerplate, slap a $5.00 price tag on it, and share…
articles.body: Impulse pricing feels like the easiest way to make your first dollar online. You ship a Notion template, an icon pack, a CLI utility, or a starter boilerplate, slap a $5.00 price tag on it, and share the checkout link. When a notification pings with a $5.00 sale, most creators mentally pocket roughly $4.50 to $4.85 . After all, payment processors advertise headline rates like 2.9% , 4% , or 10% . Then you check your payout ledger. Depending on which platform processed the checkout, between 9.0% and 31.0% of your $5.00 sale vanished into transaction fees before a single cent reached your bank account. Why? Because online payment pricing is built on a two-part equation—a percentage rate plus a fixed cent-denominated capture fee ( $0.30 to $0.80 ) .

articles.title: How an Apple Notes connector for Claude and Cursor works: permissions, limits, trade-offs
articles.excerpt: I'm the developer of NotePorter, a small Mac app ($15 one-time, up to 3 Macs, 14-day refund, 3-day full trial) that lets MCP-capable AI apps work with Apple Notes. This post explains how it works and…
articles.body: I'm the developer of NotePorter, a small Mac app ($15 one-time, up to 3 Macs, 14-day refund, 3-day full trial) that lets MCP-capable AI apps work with Apple Notes. This post explains how it works and what it deliberately does not do, because that is what I would want to know before giving an AI access to my notes. What the AI can do Search all notes and folders (full text). Read the plain text of one note. Create a note or append a line to an existing one. List notes edited in the last N days, or everything in a folder. Design choices Search reads the Notes database directly instead of driving the Notes app. Writes go through the Notes app , so iCloud sync keeps working. Never destructive. No delete, no rewrite of existing text. Appending is the only way to add to an old note.

articles.body: If you have ever helped a small business or bookkeeper do catch-up bookkeeping for a corporate credit card with multiple employee cards, you have probably seen two painful things happen: Multi-card CSV chaos in QuickBooks Online: Banks like Amex Business, Chase Ink, Capital One Spark, and Bank of America export either one combined CSV containing every employee card, separate Debit and Credit columns, or reversed signs (charges listed as positive numbers, which QuickBooks Online imports backward as payments/credits). The privacy trap: When people look for a quick statement splitter or PDF-to-CSV tool, almost every top search result asks them to upload raw client financial statements—account numbers, vendor names, dollar amounts—to a third-party cloud server or a general-purpose LLM chat.

articles.title: November’s full moon rises tonight! Here’s how to see the Beaver Moon supermoon
articles.excerpt: A dam good moon.
articles.body: Get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know. November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

articles.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
articles.excerpt: Researchers have successfully grown potatoes in simulated lunar regolith, possibly opening the door for farming on future moon bases.
articles.body: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.
